title: An unaddressed Spanish cipher letter of 8 Jan 1497, in George Lasry's reconstructed alphabet: BnF Espagnol 318 no. 95, f. 122r-v (catalogue item 9)

steps.what: No. 95 key found: Lasry's 2022 alphabet published as an image by Tomokiyo.
No. 95 f. 122r segmented and Ward-clustered, clusters labelled from Lasry's key (64 % clean clusters).
No. 95 hybrid decode checked by eye: franceses, Francia, que puedan, muy grandes cosas; about two thirds of signs; two Lasry signs corrected.
Band-clipped segmentation and DP template tiling for no. 95; no gain beyond the same two thirds.
No. 95 re-examined: cryptiana GL.htm says Lasry solved the letter itself in 2022, not just its alphabet. The page and the ranking (novelty 5 to 3) were corrected.

Split from the former whole-volume target esp318 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 95, the only letter in Lasry's alphabet, is its own entry, with his credit scoped to it. f122r_reading.md moved here; the pipeline stays in targets/esp318/.

Michael Brackx (issue #63) pointed out the second image on cryptiana GL.htm, Lasry's decipherment of ll. 1-13 (BnF_es318_f122_decipher.png), missed in Sept; NOTES had said no plaintext was published. Both images saved in targets/esp318/lit/crypt/GL/.

Brackx read ll. 14-33 and the four cipher lines of f. 122v with Lasry's alphabet, by eye on crops over about seventeen passes; proposed values for Lasry's Unknown signs and three new signs, each from two or more words; proposed nine letter corrections to Lasry's ll. 1-13. Code groups left unread, with contextual suggestions (def Maximilian I, bed cardinal).

Checked here: Lasry's image transcribed and compared with the issue's quotations of it (ll. 7, 8, 9, 10 entries are blanks over code groups or identical text, not differences); recto ll. 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 25-26 and verso l. 2 deciphered sign by sign from the scan with Lasry's table: hazen, diz, muy tarde, palabras, haga, Santa Cruz, Alemanna as Brackx has them. Brackx's ll. 14-25 agree with the project's Sept machine reading where they overlap; our l. 12 'me toca' is 'le toca'.

George Lasry's PR 75: recto transcribed in CTTS (three photographs), key from CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis (2021-22), revised with Claude Opus 5.5 (Z and R corrected) and the code groups read from context (ciudad, gente, rey, papa, cardenal; rey de romanos? tentative; five names unidentified). Edited Spanish and English translation of the whole recto.

Merged PR 75. decode.py re-applies lasry2021/ctts/key.txt: 1,323 transcribed symbols, 78 of them the two lines repeated across f122a/f122b; 1,245 once counted (1,224 letters, 2 nulls, 19 code and special signs), none unassigned, as George counts. Statistical validation (es-golden-age): -1.960 against -6.156 random (z 8.5) and -3.514 shuffled refit (z 36.7): pass. f122c overlay compared with the decode.

Lasry's 2026 recto agrees with Brackx's reading of ll. 14-33 (adopting his 'avemos traido aca'); it differs at 'rogaria a los que le ruegan' (Brackx 'logaria ... llegan'), 'para que' (Brackx 'parece que') and 'Claver avra' (Brackx 'Claue haura'). It agrees with Brackx's proposed corrections to ll. 1-13 (no ay que dezir, remitiendome, hazen, diz, con palabras, haga, no buen estado).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1226 tokens, 44 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -1.96 per letter; random keys -6.156 (z 8.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.462 (mean -3.514, z 36.7); annealer on the real text -2.095. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.96; polyphony 0.0; 19 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.095

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry recovered the alphabet with CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis from the ciphertext alone (2021-22) and completed the recto with it in 2026 (PR 75); Brackx's verso reading uses the same alphabet. No clear copy or outside key.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py --counts: all 1,245 recto symbols carry a value; the five name codes Name1-Name5 are unidentified (1240/1245). Code readings ciudad, gente, rey, papa, cardenal rest on context; rey de romanos?, aunque?, y? tentative. The four verso lines (Brackx) are outside this count.

gaps.item: five name code groups (Name1-Name5: dcl, dah, dal, dnl, boo), one occurrence each
gaps.detail: no other letter in this key is known; context suggests persons (the recipient's master, a commander) but does not name them

gaps.item: tentative readings: rey de romanos? (dif, x2; supported by the verso's Alemanna), aunque? (oN), y? (9)

gaps.detail: a burn hole according to Brackx; one image only

gaps.item: the clear date line and signature of f. 122v
gaps.detail: faded clear hand, read only as '... de enero ...'; not cipher

outcome.notes: Spanish, from an Italian city with a Signoria (Genoa fits best, per Lasry; unproved), 8 Jan 1497: famine, the French bid for the city's people, the king's slowness, the cardinal of Santa Cruz to seek peace in France, an appeal for a force to defend the city. Lasry's 2026 recto supersedes the partial 2022 overlay and settles Brackx's proposed corrections; the verso is Brackx's.

texts.label: BnF Espagnol 318 f. 122, 8 Jan 1497
texts.summary: Bread cannot be had even for money; the French court the city's silk workers with trade licences; the King provides 'muy tarde y muy poco'; the Pope wants the cardinal of Santa Cruz to seek peace in France.

prior.where: George Lasry, May 2022: cryptiana GL.htm publishes his alphabet and, as a second image, his approximate decipherment of ll. 1-13 (BnF_es318_f122_decipher.png); ll. 14-33 and the verso not published

human: George Lasry transcribed the recto in CTTS and recovered the key with its built-in cryptanalysis (2021-22), revised it with Claude Opus 5.5 and read the code groups from context (2026, PR 75). Before that: the project's segmentation reading (Sept 2026) and Michael Brackx's eye reading of ll. 14-33 and the verso (issue #63).
